references.text: Moses encourages the people to take possession of the land that the Lord has given them, addressing the same theme of entering the promised land.
Moses commissions Joshua to lead the people into the land the Lord has promised them, serving as background for Joshua's leadership.
God criticizes the people's hesitation and lack of faith in taking possession of the land, paralleling the rebuke found in Joshua.
The context for verse 3, where seven tribes had not yet received their inheritance in the land.
God's command to Joshua to be strong and courageous so that he may give the people the land as an inheritance, forming the basis for its distribution.
The judges ask Israel why they hesitate to take Lajish, reflecting a similar theme of seizing the promise of the land.
Proverbs warns against laziness and hesitation, relating to Joshua's rebuke of the tribes.
Hebrews exhorts believers not to fall short of entering God's rest, which is a spiritual parallel to the promise of the land.
